hypothesis: One decoder-reproducible Adam update after the first 32 symbols of each 64-symbol segment adapts the faithful NNCP model early enough to save at least 800 actual bytes on the exact 65536-symbol population without adding model state.
interfaces_exposed: Completed first 32 symbols -> masked causal loss -> Adam update -> decoder-rebuilt incremental KV -> remaining 32 symbols; no archive side information.
kill_condition: Any exactness failure, actual gain <800 bytes, a nonpositive chronological third, source package >65536 bytes, or decimal memory failure retires causal mid-segment split updates and higher-frequency update schedules without a split-point sweep.
promotion_condition: Two encodes and one decode are byte/state/trace identical; official inverse and joint boundary pass; archive gain versus the 96142-byte faithful parent is >=800 actual bytes; aligned chronological thirds are each positive; compressed incremental source <=65536 bytes; decimal 10GB allocated and reserved gates pass.
retired_neighborhoods: If terminal-negative, retire 32/32 split, alternative within-segment split points, and more-frequent online Adam updates at the frozen parent architecture.
title: NNCP causal 32/32 mid-segment Adam update
